A few common causes, most likely first.

1. The parent re-renders, and any function or object you pass as a prop gets rebuilt fresh each time. Even though it "looks the same," React sees a new object and treats it as changed.
2. The child isn't wrapped in `React.memo`. Without that, React re-renders it whenever the parent re-renders, no matter what the props are.
3. You're passing children as JSX built inline, which also creates a new object every render.

The fix is usually two-part: wrap the child in `React.memo`, and wrap any function or object props you pass in `useCallback` or `useMemo` so they stay the same between renders.

If you share the parent and child code, I can point to the exact line causing it.
